payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

Keep existing requirement IDs, text and exact source quotes unchanged. Add requirements only if supported by the original instruction.

parsed.text:
The graph already captures the sole requested change and appropriately distinguishes complete, partial, absent, and insufficient evidence. The main opportunity is to make the fulfillment criterion less dependent on a subjective overall impression and more consistent across repeated evaluations. The edited image shows chalk-like grain and softened, sketchy treatment across the giraffes and surroundings, while retaining substantial photographic detail; the current wording leaves room for evaluators to disagree about whether that balance counts as complete or partial.

Keep the existing requirement ID, text, and source quote unchanged. Refine the outcome target and check criteria to distinguish a genuine whole-image medium transformation from a superficial texture overlay: assess whether the giraffes and background both read as chalk-rendered, and whether photographic detail remains dominant. Make clear that visible chalk texture alone is evidence of progress, not necessarily completion; conversely, do not require every photographic detail to disappear if the image convincingly reads as a chalk drawing. Define partial as meaningful chalk treatment across some or much of the image that falls short of that whole-image reading, and reserve absent for confident evidence that no requested transformation occurred. Preserve unknown for genuinely inadequate visual evidence rather than using it to resolve borderline judgments.

Use the input and edited images explicitly as the comparison reference, and avoid adding separate requirements for particular chalk colors, exact stroke patterns, or changes to scene content, since the instruction does not specify them. A single requested check is sufficient for this one requirement; adding support checks is unlikely to improve agreement unless they provide concrete evidence that the requested check actually uses. Keep the graph within the check limit and ensure every requirement remains covered.
